posters.title:
Can a simple model choose
better experiments?
posters.deck: Aster begins with a real-data replay: predict activity, choose eight compounds, reveal their outcomes, and learn again.
posters.chart_title: SARS-CoV-2 Mpro · discovery after 40 additional picks
posters.axis: Additional assay hits per 40 picks · pIC50 ≥ 6
steps: 1,328 rows → 922 eligible compounds; preserve the published train/test split.
200 trees fit only the measurements revealed so far.
100 initial results; five batches of eight; compare with random picks.
posters.evaluation: 712 compounds for training/acquisition; 210 held out for audit. Ten paired seeds, the same 40-pick budget, and hidden-label checks. This is a retrospective single-target experiment.
posters.takeaway: The baseline chose many more assay hits than random. Random had slightly lower audit error (0.748 vs 0.793): prediction accuracy and useful selection are different objectives.
sources: [2–3] RDKit + scikit-learn · Morgan fingerprints and random forests
posters.note: ASSAY HIT ≠ A SAFE OR EFFECTIVE DRUG

posters.title:
The harder test:
does deep learning help?
posters.deck: Challenge the baseline with less starting data, unfamiliar chemical scaffolds, and frozen CheMeleon representations.
posters.chart_title: Two evaluation targets · mean discovery after 40 picks
posters.axis: Compounds found from the pool’s strongest 10% / 40 picks
steps: One development target; two evaluation targets. Freeze rules first.
Morgan bits versus 2,048 frozen CheMeleon features.
Separate starting chemistry, acquisition pool and audit scaffolds.
Three seeds; two starting sizes; five batches of eight.
posters.evaluation: Three tasks × two protocols × two starting sizes × three seeds × four arms = 144 replays. Chart uses androgen/glucocorticoid receptor tasks only; they share 133 molecular identities.
posters.takeaway: No clear overall neural advantage. CheMeleon also had severe prediction failures: mean final audit MAE 5.60. Investigate the head before adding complexity.
sources: [2–3] RDKit + scikit-learn · Aster replay protocol, not an official leaderboard
posters.note: PRETRAINING OVERLAP UNRESOLVED · NO UNIVERSAL WINNER

posters.title:
Stable predictions.
No neural advantage yet.
posters.deck: Repair the prediction head on development data, freeze it, then test additional targets and a matched fine-tuning pilot.
posters.axis: Compounds found from the pool’s strongest 10% / 40 picks
steps: Compare centering, a variance floor, feature filtering and ridge strength.
Drop observed feature SD <0.01; scale retained features; ridge α=10.
Serotonin 1A, GSK-3β and CLK4; remove exposed-target overlaps.
Five epochs per round on observed labels; refit the same ridge policy.
posters.evaluation: 108 development +96 fresh-target +6 tuned replays. Same starting measurements and 40-pick budgets within each comparison. Filters fit observed data only; no prediction clipping.
posters.takeaway: Matched six-case pilot: frozen 15.33 → tuned 13.67 discoveries. Four ties, two losses. Keep Morgan/ridge provisional; this specific adaptation recipe did not help.
sources: [4–5] MoleculeACE · fixed Ki tasks and scaffold tests
[6–8,11] CheMeleon + Chemprop + PyTorch · pretrained encoder and custom adaptation
[2–3] RDKit + scikit-learn · training-only transforms and ridge regression
posters.note: STABILITY FIXED IN THESE TESTS · FINE-TUNING RESULT IS A SMALL PILOT

posters.title:
Which uncertainty signals
actually help us choose?
posters.deck: Test disagreement, chemical novelty and batch diversity while keeping the same molecules, starting data and measurement budget.
posters.chart_title: Three fresh targets · frozen primary policy and controls
posters.axis: Compounds found from the pool’s strongest 10% / 40 picks
steps: Morgan + ridge α=10; no neural tuning in this milestone.
16 bootstrap fits; nearest measured Tanimoto neighbor; CV residual bands.
Greedy, explore, cautious, diverse, hybrid, forest and random.
84 development and 168 fresh-target replays; inspect exact score traces.
posters.evaluation: Under greedy: disagreement error-AUC 0.477; novelty AUC 0.610 (chance =0.5). Nominal-80% bands covered 72.5%; sigma scaffold cases only 63.4%.
posters.takeaway: Exploration 14.17 vs greedy 14.29: no improvement. Diversity gained +0.83, below the +1 threshold. Novelty is a weak diagnostic; disagreement is not calibrated confidence.
sources: [4–5] MoleculeACE · dopamine transporter, sigma receptor 1 and PI3Kα tasks
[2–3,10] RDKit + scikit-learn · Tanimoto, ridge, CV and audit metrics
posters.note: SECONDARY DIVERSITY SIGNAL IS EXPLORATORY · NO PAID COMPUTE
